verdict.rationale: MoQ is library-first: its only documented UI, the `<moq-watch>` player element, is an optional layer over the @moq/watch library. Subscribing and publishing are also exposed through Rust and TypeScript libraries, FFI bindings and a CLI, so the UI's functions appear to be reachable programmatically. No source states API/UI parity, and there is no documented relay management or admin API; the OpenAPI probes all returned 404. missing for 10: an explicit statement that the API matches the UI, a documented relay administration/management API (OpenAPI or equivalent), independent confirmation that no UI-only functions exist.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Subscribe to and render MoQ broadcasts, with an optional `<moq-watch>` UI.
Libraries for Rust (native) and TypeScript (web), plus FFI bindings for C, Python, Kotlin, Swift, Go, and Dart.
A CLI that can import and publish MoQ broadcasts from a variety of formats (fMP4, HLS, MPEG-TS, FLV, etc), including via ffmpeg.
